claim: SPIRE concepts page: each agent must authenticate the node on first connection (node attestation) by join token ('a pre-shared key'), cloud instance identity (AWS/Azure/GCE), Kubernetes service-account tokens or an existing X.509 certificate; workload attestation then asks the kernel or kubelet 'who is this process'; the server signs X.509- and JWT-SVIDs and agents cache them

SPIRE v1.16.0 ships server node attestors aws_iid, azure_imds, azure_msi, gcp_iit, http_challenge, join_token, k8s_psat, sshpop, tpm_devid and x509pop; tpm_devid needs a DevID (LDevID) certificate provisioned 'through an out-of-band mechanism', the DevID CA and the TPM manufacturer endorsement CA, and issues a proof-of-possession challenge and a proof-of-residency challenge (key generated in and resident in a TPM whose endorsement certificate chains to a trusted manufacturer CA)

FIDO Alliance FDO overview: FDO is an 'automatic onboarding protocol for edge nodes, datacenter servers, and IoT devices'; the page refers to the 'current FDO v2.0 specification' and links v1.1; late binding 'allows devices to be manufactured without first identifying the end customer'; 'a local rendezvous server permits onboarding to closed networks'; a certification program covers devices, onboarding services and rendezvous servers; open-source Go, Rust and C implementations are in LF Edge

Matter SDK (connectedhomeip v1.6.1.0, Apache-2.0): devices carry Device Attestation Certificates (DACs) chained through Product Attestation Intermediates (PAIs), and a commissioner checks them against a revocation set during commissioning (device-attestation revocation guide); the SDK ships fabric-admin, fabric-bridge, fabric-sync and joint-fabric examples for several administrators of one device; the CSA Matter page cites 'enhanced multi-admin support across ecosystems' and 'NFC tap-to-pair'
